bottom_line_fact.text: The Cboe 3-month implied correlation index sits at 11.2 versus a long-run average of 41, and only ~43% of S&P 500 stocks are above their 200-day average (down from 75% in mid-August), indicating unusually low correlation and narrow breadth.

bottom_line_inference.text: With bonds offering weaker diversification amid a positive stock-bond correlation, the article argues the diversification opportunity has shifted inside equities, raising the payoff to sector and thematic stock selection rather than index exposure.

structural_view.text: The article frames a regime shift in which the historical bond diversifier is weaker, making within-equity dispersion a durable source of diversification.

hypotheses.title: Low stock correlation makes sector and thematic selection the key diversifier within equities

transmission_chain.text: Positive stock-bond correlation reduces bonds' diversification value, pushing investors to seek diversification within equities.

bottom_line_fact.text: S&P 500 Utilities swung from a July peak above 10% to around -10% price return since May as datacenter moratoriums (New York, then Texas in early August) and rising Treasury yields weighed on the sector.

bottom_line_inference.text: The article treats utilities as both an AI enabler and a victim of political backlash and higher rates; the net effect on the sector has been sharply negative, though the article does not quantify an earnings impact, only price and P/E declines.

hypotheses.title: Rate rise and datacenter moratoriums have pressured utilities exposed to the AI trade

transmission_chain.text: AI datacenter build-out requires large electricity supply, making utilities key enablers of AI.
Rising reliance on utilities raised electricity prices for consumers, triggering political backlash and state moratoriums on build-out.

Moratoriums curtail the build-out that would drive utilities' volume growth, and higher Treasury yields erode the relative appeal of utilities' dividends; the article shows resulting price and P/E declines but does not quantify earnings.
S&P 500 Utilities fell from above 10% to around -10% price return since May, with P/E compressing after the moratorium announcements.

unknowns: Whether moratoriums are temporary or durable and how much they actually curtail utilities' AI-driven demand growth
Whether utilities' earnings (not just P/E and price) have been impaired
